bib.title: Improving Retrieval Augmented Language Model with Self-Reasoning
bib.venue: AAAI 2025 (inferred from 'Copyright © 2025, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence'; no venue name printed; arXiv:2407.19813v3 [cs.CL], 19 Dec 2024)

question: Can an LLM be trained to produce its own reasoning trajectories (relevance judgement, cited evidence snippets, analysis) so a RAG model is more robust to irrelevant retrieval and gives traceable citations, without external modules?
hypothesis: Explicit self-generated reasoning trajectories over retrieved documents improve retrieval robustness and answer accuracy.
contributions: End-to-end Self-Reasoning framework needing no external tools
Three processes (RAP, EAP, TAP) giving interpretability and traceability via snippets and citations
Evaluation on four public datasets beating prior SOTA with only 2,000 training samples

method.summary: LLaMA2 7B/13B is fine-tuned on 2,000 GPT-4 generated, filtered trajectories. In one pass the model emits a relevance judgement (RAP), cited evidence snippets with reasons (EAP), then an analysis (long answer) and short answer (TAP). Training is staged with masking (gradual learning).
method.task: retrieval-augmented QA (short-form, long-form with citations) and fact verification

datasets.name: Self-reasoning training set
datasets.size: 10,000 GPT-4 samples generated, 2,000 kept after filtering
datasets.source: GPT-4 generated; questions drawn from training sets of the evaluated tasks (not stated in detail)
datasets.preprocessing: RAP negatives: random other question's top-k docs paired with the question; document order shuffled; filtered by answer correctness and, for long-form, citation recall and precision >= 0.8

datasets.name: PopQA
datasets.source: Mallen et al. 2023; Dec 2020 Wikipedia corpus from Izacard et al. 2022

models.name: Self-Reasoning 7B / 13B
models.init_from: LLaMA-2 7B and 13B (base, per 'fine-tune the LLaMA-2 model')

training.objective: max E log p(y | tau, q) p(tau | q), standard LM likelihood over trajectory plus answer; stage-wise masking: stage 1 masks EAP and TAP, stage 2 masks TAP, stage 3 trains on all

other.epochs_note: unclear whether 3 epochs per stage or total

inference.samples: Table 1 averaged over five runs, std <= 2%
inference.prompting: Baselines zero-shot on short-form QA, one-shot on long-form QA and FEVER
inference.retrieval: top-5 docs from Wikipedia; DPR (NQ), Contriever-MS MARCO (PopQA, Dec 2020 Wikipedia), GTR (ASQA)

other.note: greedy decoding with temperature 0.2 both stated

metrics.name: accuracy (short-form QA)
metrics.definition: ground-truth answer included in prediction, not exact match

metrics.name: EM recall
metrics.definition: ASQA correctness metric from Gao et al. 2023b

metrics.name: citation recall / precision
metrics.definition: ALCE NLI-based automatic citation metrics; human version on 100 ASQA samples, 2 annotators each

eval.protocol: Five runs averaged; noise test shuffles order and replaces 50% of retrieved docs with docs from another question; human citation eval on 100 ASQA samples

prompts.purpose: GPT-4 instruction to generate trajectories for short-form and long-form QA
prompts.text:
# Role
You are an experienced expert, skilled in answering various questions.
# Task
Please answer the question according to the provided reference evidence as required.
# Reference Evidence
[1] Retrieved Document {{DOCUMENT 1}} ... [5] Retrieved Document {{DOCUMENT 5}}
# Requirements
1. First, please judge whether the provided documents are relevant with the question, and put it in the relevant field. If the provided content is irrelevant to the question, explain the reason in the relevant reason field, then you can give the answer with your internal knowledge.
2. If possible, answer the question in points and provide explanations.
3. If the content in the answer comes from different pieces of evidence, you need to cite the sequence number of the evidence at the end of the sentence. The citation format is shown below: [1], [1,3].
4. Place each cited piece of evidence in the cite_list field, cite content field to store each paragraph of cited content (omitted words can be replaced by ...), cite reason is used to store your thoughts and analysis of this content, how this paragraph can answer the question.
5. Put the long answer content in the analysis field, and put the short answer(no more than 10 words) in the answer field.
# Question
{{QUESTION}}

terms.definition: Relevance-Aware Process: LLM judges whether retrieved documents are relevant and gives a reason
Evidence-Aware Selective Process: LLM chooses and cites relevant documents, selects key-sentence snippets and gives reason
Trajectory Analysis Process: LLM synthesizes analysis (long answer) and short answer from previous trajectories
